siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred butcher's household (1 of 1 this layer infers): hh_inf_butcher_south_01 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: The Clybourn household — a documented butcher in a reconstructed household (south division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d5_011 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.

persons.name: A. Clybourn
persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON IN A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD, AND THE TWO HALVES OF THAT ARE GRADED SEPARATELY. The person is real and the papers name him: 1833-12-10 c003 (p. 1, col. 1), and 5 mention(s) between 1833-12-10 and 1834-12-24. WHERE HE LIVED AND WORKED IS STILL RECONSTRUCTED — the dwelling, the workplace and the division on this record are the ones the inferred-household programme dealt to the invented resident this replaces, and NOTHING HERE CLAIMS THEY ARE HIS. No source this project holds gives him an address; if one did, the register would have placed him and tools/retire_invented_residents.py would have refused him for that reason (refusal 5). This is what T-0264 retires: the town raised this household because it demonstrably needed the trade and had nobody documented to put in it, and it now has somebody. The invented name and its `name_basis` are gone with the invention. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1); the liberty taken is the housing, not the man.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - first of 1 butcher households in this layer, in the south division. One butcher is documented: Clybourne, the government butcher, who is also a packer and lives three kilometres out on the North Branch. A town of 3,265 buys fresh meat daily and does not walk to the North Branch for it. One butchering household is inferred, keeping a market shop on the built streets. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
